decisive_items: Monomorphic, perivascular, and periadnexal atypical lymphocytic infiltrate
Phenotypically abnormal T-cell population with CD52 expression
Epidermal necrosis with numerous fibrin thrombi and intra-/perivascular atypical lymphocytic infiltrate showing monotony and hyperchromasia
response.rationale: Pathology and flow cytometry show atypical T-cell infiltrate with abnormal phenotype, diagnostic of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Pyoderma gangrenosum is clinically plausible but lacks histologic support.

rejected.why: Oral/genital ulcers are nonspecific and not supported by biopsy findings.
Vasculitis is suggested by purpura but contradicted by atypical lymphocytic infiltrate.
Ulcer morphology fits but biopsy shows lymphocytic atypia, not neutrophilic dermatosis.
